purpose: When any offload tool changes, make the other applicable tools deterministically inspect, compare, verify, sandbox, rebuild, and refresh that tool and then reciprocally process the peer stack; only after the whole peer graph passes may generated artifacts and stack metadata be promoted, while AI retains intent judgment.

requirements.statement: A changed tool is checked by every applicable peer role and the candidate reciprocally processes every applicable peer before stack promotion.
Previous active capabilities are preserved: baseline functional contracts must pass in addition to delta feature acceptance.
Verification, acceptance evidence, intent assessment, and release are bound to the exact candidate artifact SHA-256.
Feature acceptance contracts without a mandatory locked_sha256 and an external pre-implementation pin must not be promotable.
Opaque/native executable scenarios must not execute directly on the host when strong sandbox evidence is required; they must be sandboxed or BLOCKED.

Peer update automation must not mutate peer source code or partially promote stack metadata; updates are limited to generated artifacts/evidence/metadata and are committed atomically after all required gates pass.
Any peer failure, missing required artifact, contract drift, or inconclusive mandatory gate prevents promotion and leaves the prior active state authoritative.
Executable changes are generically detected and require a feature-acceptance contract rather than relying on hard-coded tool names.
Machine output uses PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, and INCONCLUSIVE without converting unavailable verification into PASS.
Programs return deterministic facts and update mechanics only; they do not decide whether user intent is satisfied.
